2.text: When the first child has died young, it is considered to have traced the

3.text: way for the following ones. In order to stop this fatal succession, the incan-

4.text: tation must be performed as soon as possible. The care of the matter falls

5.text: on the father of the child, and it is most propitious if he himself is able to

6.text: perform the ceremony. If he is not able, he invites some of his experienced

7.text: relatives, who can name several “knowing people” possessed of the incantation

8.text: in question. These latter are more frequently male than female. The choice

9.text: of the performer is indicated by divination with a suspended object, in the

10.text: usual way. Then the husband goes to seek the designated person, who may

11.text: be more than fifty miles away. As said before, the “knowing man” must at

12.text: first refuse, and he may persist in this refusal for even three or four days,

13.text: to avoid the displeasure of the Deity. The negotiations are carried on in

14.text: whispers, in the strictest secrecy, and only inside of the sleeping-room.

15.text: The best time of all for performing the ceremony is during the first

16.text: three days of the young moon, but, nevertheless, in the day-time. For this

17.text: a small fire is built up before the entrance, and a number of plates laden

18.text: with various meats, cooked or dried, are placed on both sides of it. The

19.text: performer gives each of the parents a small piece of red stone wrapped in

20.text: leather formed into a necklace. Then he pronounces an incantation, of which

21.text: the following may serve as a fair specimen: —

22.text: “You are not on this earth; you are within this stone. No wind may reach you; no iceberg

23.text: may crush you, but it will break into pieces against the edges of the stone. You are not on this

24.text: earth. In the open ocean there lies a big sea-animal born at the same time with the earth and the

25.text: world. This animal is a sea-lion. Its back is like an island, it is covered with earth and stones.

27.text: A similar necklace is put, with the same incantation, on the child’s neck.

28.text: The performer takes the child in his arms, and makes three rounds among

29.text: the plates of meat, stepping over them forward and backward, and retracing

30.text: his steps, in order to make his trail more intricate. Then the fire and the

31.text: principal “directions” are fed from the plates. What remains of the meat is

32.text: eaten by those present. The lobes of the child’s ears are pierced, and ear-

33.text: ornaments, each made of three small colored beads, are inserted. Several

34.text: additional figures of “guardians,” made of leather, are sewed to the child’s

35.text: garment. Its name is also changed.

36.text: EXPOSURE OF INFANTS. — Sarytcheff says that in his time the Chukchee

37.text: exposed their misshaped infants.² I have said before, that I know of no such

38.text: practice in modern times.³ But in the case of a lying-in woman dying in

39.text: her labors, the babe is often smothered and exposed, together with the mother,

41.text: ² Sarytcheff, II, p. 109. Steller mentions that the Kamchadal women of his time had many ways of producing

42.text: abortion, but that, not satisfied with this, they often also smothered their babes, and then gave the corpses to the

43.text: dogs, or exposed them alive in the middle of the wood (p. 349).
